extracted.intended_audience: poets submitting speculative/genre poetry to Strange Horizons
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for poets on submitting poetry (science fiction, fantasy, horror, mythology, supernatural, or science/technology–inflected) to the online magazine Strange Horizons, including format, rights, editorial preferences, and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: What We Publish (subject matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: We publish poems with a science fiction, fantasy, horror, mythology, supernatural, or science/technology element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can read nearly every poem Strange Horizons has published since 2000 in the archives to get a sense of suitable work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay rate and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Our pay rate for new poetry is $50 (U.S.) per poem, regardless of length or complexity. We buy first-English-language worldwide exclusive print rights for six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment and rights apply per poem; after the six-month exclusive print period, rights revert as per normal publishing practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission system and acceptable file types
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use our Moksha submissions system to send us your poems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We accept Text files (.txt), RTF files (.rtf), Word 97–2003 Documents (.doc), Word Documents (.docx), and PDF file types (.pdf).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of poems per submission
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than six (6) poems at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All poems may be in one file or in separate files — both formats are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter and word count fields importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t worry about the cover letter or word count fields. They will almost never influence our decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if your poem draws substantially on another work (centos, golden shovels, erasures; riffs on fairy tales, TV shows, books), please identify the relevant works in the cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously unpublished work requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We don’t run unsolicited reprints. If it was previously in print and available to readers — offline or online, including on personal websites or message boards — then it’s been published. We will consider previously unpublished English-language translations of work that has been published in another language if the original author is on board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your poem is acquired by another publisher before we reply to you, then please withdraw your poem using the Moksha system. If you submitted the poem in a file with other poems and can’t withdraw it without withdrawing all of them, then please email us about it.

rubrics_metrics.name: No auto-generated text / AI policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We expect you to actively select each word you use in your poem. Individual editors also explicitly state they do not want submissions written or translated by, or with the assistance of, AI/LLMs/chat bots/etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time / reply timeframe
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you haven’t heard from us by the time the four-month mark passes, please email us, because that means your reply was probably lost in our spam filter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading periods and editor jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poetry Department is open year-round; editors operate on a rotation system and the person who reads and replies to your poem depends on when you send it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each editor has jurisdiction over work submitted in their reading periods. Romie and AJ are senior in tenure but do not review or overrule decisions made by Lisa or Vanessa. You can address a submission to a specific editor or simply 'Dear Editors.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor preference — AJ Odasso
rubrics_metrics.description: AJ Odasso's submission preference and prohibitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please don’t send me poems generated or translated by AI tools, chat bots, LLMs, or similar. AJ wants verse that’s drawn from what drives you, fascinates you, excites you, obsesses you, grieves you—what you absolutely need to put on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor preference — Lisa M. Bradley
rubrics_metrics.description: Lisa Bradley's submission preference and dislikes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I do not want submissions written or translated by, or with the assistance of, AI/LLMs/chat bots/etc. Also, she receives lots of mermaid, mushroom, and Little Red Riding Hood poems, so those are a hard sell now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor preference — Romie Stott
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Romie notes they are probably the slowest to respond of all the editors; this is not personal (logistical expectation rather than content criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor preference — Vanessa Jae
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vanessa is looking for intensely human poetry: raw emotions with experimental structures, beautiful words describing unspoken experiences. Be ruthlessly you and share it with me (and the world). She also notes she never gets enough science fiction poems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and reuse notice
rubrics_metrics.description: All material in Strange Horizons is copyrighted to the original authors and may not be reproduced without permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard copyright notice: authors retain copyright; reproduction requires permission.
